sections.name: VoiceRecorderButtonProps (part 1)
sections.title: Inputs, online tracking and starting a recording
sections.what: Defines what the button accepts and keeps its state: recording, transcribing, timer, online status and error message. It listens for the browser's online and offline events. Starting clears old errors, stops if offline, then asks for the microphone and begins recording.
sections.why: Likely reason: transcription needs a network connection, so the browser's online status decides whether the button can be used.
sections.watch_out: The browser's online status can be wrong on some networks, so a request may still fail even when the button is enabled.

sections.name: VoiceRecorderButtonProps (part 2)
sections.title: Stopping, uploading and the timer
sections.what: When recording stops, collects the audio pieces into one webm file, releases the microphone, and uploads the file. Shows the server's error or passes the returned text to the parent. Ticks the timer every second and formats the seconds as minutes and seconds.
sections.why: Likely reason: the audio is sent once, as a whole clip, after recording ends.
sections.watch_out: The audio is not stored anywhere, so if the upload fails the recording is gone.

sections.name: VoiceRecorderButtonProps: if
sections.title: Button looks for each state
sections.what: Shows four looks: a disabled offline button, a spinner while transcribing, a red pulsing stop button with elapsed time while recording, and the normal start button with any error message. Compact mode hides the text label.
sections.why: Likely reason: clear feedback at each stage so the user knows what the button is doing.
sections.watch_out: The error message appears only in the normal start view, so a failure is seen only after the spinner ends.

summary: A microphone button that records a short voice clip, sends it to the server for transcription, and passes the returned text back.
purpose: Lets the user dictate notes or tasks instead of typing.
why: Likely reason: the button's tooltip names Groq Whisper, so transcription runs on the server and the browser only records and uploads.
how: Checks whether the device is online. On click, asks for microphone permission and starts recording while a timer counts seconds. Clicking stop ends the recording, packages the audio as a webm file, sends it to the transcribe endpoint, and passes the returned text to the parent. It shows a spinner while waiting and an error message if something fails.
inputs: The callback that receives text, optional styling, a compact flag and a button label; microphone audio; the browser's online status.
outputs: A call to the callback with the transcribed text, status messages on screen, and an audio upload to the transcribe endpoint.
risks: Audio is not kept, so a failed upload loses the recording. Any microphone error is reported as denied, even when the cause is different. When offline the button is disabled, with only a tooltip to explain why.
debug: If the button stays disabled, check the browser's online status. If 'Mic access denied' appears, check the browser's microphone permission and that a microphone exists. If transcription fails, check the transcribe route and the error it returns, and the browser console for network failures.
